title: Large Language Model and Formal Concept Analysis: a comparative study for Topic Modeling
subcategory: comparison: formal concept analysis vs prompted LLM
task: Topic extraction from small domain corpora (course materials, research papers)
problem: Little applied evidence on whether LLMs or Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) suit topic modelling, and what each trades off.
architecture: CREA pipeline: BabelFy entity linking, POS filtering, term binarisation with beta coefficients (direct/medium/high/low strategies), FCA concept lattice, Ward hierarchical agglomerative clustering with k chosen by internal indices. LLM side: GPT-5 zero-shot, three prompts (topic generation per batch of 1-10 documents, merging into 5 final topics, labelling).
llm_or_encoder: GPT-5 (topic generation); ChatGPT for labelling CREA topics

datasets.name: PHP dataset
datasets.details: French course documents used in earlier CREA work; 8 sessions

datasets.name: Abstracts / Full Papers
datasets.details: 40 information-systems research articles; abstracts 3,343 tokens, full papers 223,530 tokens

key_results: PHP data, medium strategy (beta = 1.25): k = 5 gives Silhouette 0.46, CHI 12.76, Dunn 0.79, DBI 0.91, chosen as the trade-off.
CREA clusters are strongly imbalanced on abstracts (e.g. largest cluster 361 terms vs 27 for the second at beta = 1.00, k = 8, medium strategy).
GPT-5 produced balanced, readable topics with a logical progression, while CREA kept finer technical terms (e.g. mysqli, varchar).
strengths: Direct comparison of a transparent, deterministic pipeline with a black-box LLM on the same corpora.
Discusses reproducibility, privacy and parameter burden explicitly.

limitations.text: Small, domain-specific datasets; exploratory rather than a definitive comparison.
CREA needs heavy parameter tuning, scales poorly (lattice growth) and its imbalance prevented use of classical coherence measures.
LLM results are not reproducible and the model is a black box.
No quantitative score compares GPT-5 topics with the IS subfields or with CREA.
